method_notes: TASK A - BUSINESS-EVENT CAPABILITY AT SPORT VENUES. Read the census venues.json programmatically and extracted the 531 records whose venue_type is RACECOURSE, FOOTBALL_STADIUM, RUGBY_STADIUM, CRICKET_GROUND, INDOOR_ARENA or MOTORSPORT_CIRCUIT, plus their canonical_name/city/alternative_names, as the Task A candidate pool. Because the census already holds 811 venues including the whole purpose-built conference/exhibition estate (ExCeL, Olympia London, The ICC Birmingham, Telford International Centre, Harrogate Convention Centre, Manchester Central, Scottish Event Campus, P&J Live, ICC Belfast, ICC Wales, Bournemouth International Centre, Brighton Centre and others), the gap this workstream addresses is specifically the business-event layer inside sport venues. Examined in depth: 30 sport venues - 8 racecourses (Cheltenham, Doncaster, Aintree, Sandown Park, Newbury, Epsom Downs, Ascot, York), 13 football stadiums (Wembley, Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, Emirates, Stamford Bridge, Old Trafford, Etihad, Anfield, St James' Park, Villa Park, Elland Road, Ashton Gate, London Stadium, Hampden Park, Principality Stadium), 3 rugby stadiums (Allianz Stadium Twickenham, Scottish Gas Murrayfield, Sandy Park) and 5 cricket grounds (Emirates Old Trafford, Lord's, The Kia Oval, Edgbaston, Trent Bridge). Representation: exactly ONE (A1) separate sub-venue record was created - The Centaur at Cheltenham Racecourse - because it is the only sport-venue business-event facility found that is separately named, separately marketed on its own web estate AND separately calendared with its own public what's-on of named forthcoming events. Every other venue is recorded as (A2) business-event capability against the parent, re-listed with the exact canonical_name and city from venues.json and with the principal capacity deliberately null + CAPACITY_REVIEW_REQUIRED so the parent's proven spectator capacity is not displaced. Two sport-venue conference complexes were checked and found ALREADY HELD as separate census records, so no new record was made: Silverstone International Conference and Exhibition Centre (already a sub-venue of Silverstone Circuit) and Coventry Building Society Arena (already a MULTI_PURPOSE_EVENT_COMPLEX parent with its Indoor Arena as a sub-venue; its 6,000 sqm exhibition halls therefore already sit inside the census). SCHEMA CAVEAT: the workstream record schema's venue_type enum has no CRICKET_GROUND value, although cricket grounds were in scope as Task A candidates. The five cricket-ground (A2) records therefore carry venue_type MULTI_PURPOSE_EVENT_COMPLEX as the closest allowed value, and each one states in scale_description that the census parent's type is CRICKET_GROUND and that this is not a reclassification claim. The compiler should not treat these as venue_type election evidence. CALENDAR FINDING (the hire-page distinction): of the 30 sport venues examined, only 7 publish a genuine listing of named forthcoming BUSINESS or non-sport events - The Centaur (Cheltenham), Doncaster Racecourse, Sandown Park, Aintree, Epsom Downs, Ascot and Sandy Park. All 7 are recorded with calendar_sources. The other 23 publish venue-hire marketing only: capacity charts, floor plans, room galleries and enquiry forms, with their public what's-on covering stadium-bowl sport and concerts that the census already captures. That is the expected and honest result - conference, exhibition and banqueting bookings at stadiums are overwhelmingly private corporate events that are never published - and each such record carries a no_public_calendar_reason instead of a fabricated calendar. No hire page, capacity chart or enquiry form was recorded as a calendar.  TASK B - SHOWGROUND ESTATE AUDIT. Established programmatically that the census already held 17 permanent agricultural-society showgrounds: South of England Event Centre (Ardingly), Westpoint Exeter (Devon County Showground), Great Yorkshire Events Centre (Harrogate), Trinity Park (Ipswich/Suffolk), NAEC Stoneleigh, Lincolnshire Showground, Kent Event Centre (Detling), Three Counties Showground (Malvern), Newark Showground, Norfolk Showground, East of England Arena and Events Centre (Peterborough), Royal Bath & West Showground, Staffordshire County Showground, Royal Cornwall Events Centre, Eikon Exhibition Centre / Balmoral Park (Royal Ulster), Royal Highland Centre (Ingliston) and Royal Welsh Showground (Builth Wells). ASAO NEGATIVE FINDING: ASAO does not publish a member directory of shows or showgrounds. asao.co.uk/members/ returns HTTP 404, and the live directory at asao.co.uk/organisations/ lists only 8 organisations on the page (Welsh Pony & Cob Society, British Show Jumping, NFYFC, National Sheep Association, North West Federation of Show Societies, Royal Agricultural Society of England, Royal Windsor Show and London International Horse Show, Yeovil Agricultural Society) - none of which is a showground census. Wikipedia has no "List of agricultural shows in the United Kingdom" article (HTTP 404). The estate therefore had to be enumerated society-by-society from Wikipedia's agricultural-show categories and then corroborated against each society's own site; there is no authoritative national register to check against, which is itself the central limit on any completeness claim here. ADDED: 14 permanent showgrounds absent from the census - England: Cheshire Showground (Tabley/Knutsford), Newbury Showground, Westmorland County Show Ground (Crooklands), The West Mid Showground (Shrewsbury), Hertfordshire County Showground (Redbourn), Driffield Showground, Bakewell Showground. Wales: The Anglesey Showground (Gwalchmai/Mona), Carmarthen Showground (Nantyci), Monmouthshire Showground, Haverfordwest Showground (Pembrokeshire). Scotland: Borders Events Centre (Springwood Park, Kelso), Mannsfield Showground (Black Isle, Muir of Ord), The Haughs (Turriff). Northern Ireland: nothing further qualified beyond Balmoral Park, already held. The single most significant miss was the Borders Events Centre at Kelso - a 1,000 sqm purpose-built function hall seating 1,000 theatre style on a 40-acre permanent showground, with a live public events calendar. It is the largest permanent agricultural-society events building in Scotland after the Royal Highland Centre. EXCLUDED with reasons: Essex County Showground, Great Leighs (converted to a racecourse in 2008, no longer a society showground); Weedon Park, Aylesbury (Bucks County Show - society-held show field, no venue-hire or events offer found); New Park, Brockenhurst (New Forest Show - permanent ground but the society publishes no venue-hire or year-round events offer); Stoke Park, Guildford (Surrey County Show - council public park); North Somerset Agricultural Society (no showground venue identity; the show is moving site in 2027); Dorset County Show, Dorchester (no showground name, operator or hire offer published); Dorset Show Ground at West Stour (a private family equestrian centre, not an agricultural society showground - not to be confused with the Dorset County Show); Moreton Show, Honiton Show and Turnpike Showground, Motcombe (permanent or society-owned but no year-round venue business published - Honiton in particular is a genuine borderline, a society-owned 140-acre site with a show-only web presence); Denbigh & Flint, Dumfries (show fields); Clogher Valley Show and Omagh Show / Tyrone Farming Society in Northern Ireland (permanent grounds but single annual shows with no hire offer or what's-on); Ballymena Showgrounds (a council football stadium, already in the census as such); Nantwich (Dorfold Hall), Northumberland County Show (Bywell), Cumberland Show (Carlisle Racecourse), Newport Show (Chetwynd Deer Park), Vale of Glamorgan (Fonmon Castle) and Tendring Hundred (Lawford) - all staged on rented estate or racecourse land with no persistent venue identity. UNRESOLVED / COULD NOT FETCH: Royal Lancashire Show (royallancashireshow.org.uk does not resolve - historically a moving show); Stithians Show, Cornwall (TLS handshake failure); Keith Show, Moray (no response); Yeovil Agricultural Society, an actual ASAO member, whose domain now resolves to an unrelated commercial site. Thainstone Centre, Inverurie was considered and set aside as a commercial livestock-mart/exhibition centre operated by ANM Group rather than an agricultural society showground, but it was not fetched. VERDICT ON THE SHOWGROUND ESTATE: with 17 already held plus 14 added, the census now carries 31 permanent UK showgrounds and I judge the estate PLAUSIBLE BUT NOT PROVEN COMPLETE. Every large first-tier county/royal showground I could identify from society sources is now present in England, Wales and Scotland, and Northern Ireland's single qualifying ground was already held. The remaining risk is concentrated in the second tier - county societies that own a permanent ground but market it only as a show site - where the inclusion boundary is genuinely a judgement call, and in the four sites above that could not be fetched at all. I did NOT establish completeness: no national register of showgrounds exists to check against, ASAO publishes no member list, and the enumeration therefore rests on society-by-society discovery which cannot be proved exhaustive. Scotland and Wales are the thinnest coverage and would repay a further pass.  EVIDENCE DISCIPLINE: every capacity, square-metre, acreage, address and postcode in this file was read on a page I fetched myself, and the exact URL is cited in capacity_source and/or evidence. Where a first-party page published no figure, the field is null rather than filled from a third-party directory - notably Carmarthen (official 52 acres, not the 100 acres third parties quote), Anglesey (official 136 acres, not 160) and Pembrokeshire (no official figures at all, so the widely quoted 60 acres and Pavilion 250/400 capacities are deliberately NOT recorded). Allianz Stadium Twickenham carries a first-party "over 7,000 sqm" total against a trade-body "12,000m2"; the first-party figure is recorded and the conflict is noted. Sites that block plain HTTP fetchers (unitedcounties.org returns 403, pembsshow.org returns malformed headers) and calendars delivered through cross-origin widgets (Driffield) were read in a real browser. Latitude and longitude are null throughout.
